original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: For two dirty registers and the 24 paid rank-one shears over F2[UT3(F3)] generated by x, x^-1, y, y^-1, is the exact minimum call count for diag([z],[z]) equal to the eight-call direct schedule, where z=[x,y]?
scope_change_reason: The selector card allows one specified nonabelian address group. The first candidate Q16 was released after direct pricing showed x^4=y^2, so two targets cost four calls. This refinement uses the order-27 exponent-three Heisenberg group, where its central commutator has shortest generator word length four and the two-target direct bill is eight.
bottleneck_link: A shorter exact nonabelian register word could lower a bit primitive call count. The exact eight-call lower bound rules out this particular cross-register mechanism in a changed address group; it does not alter the selected supplier or kappa.
stop_rule: Exhaust exact product states at every word length 0 through 7 over all 24 operations (six rank-one idempotents times four generator labels). Compare against the explicit eight-call word and stop there. Do not vary group, register count, target, or operation prices in this cycle.
evidence: python3 -B research/heisenberg-central-pair-seed0154/verify.py passes. It constructs exact F2[UT3(F3)] product-state layers, proves no endpoint match for lengths 0..7 by complete meet-in-the-middle, and verifies the direct length-8 witness. Layer state counts are 1, 24, 413, 5927, 82063 with pinned SHA-256 receipts; six controls and 144 optimized-versus-literal matrix checks pass.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: OpenAI Codex provided substantial assistance with the scope screening, exact model, exhaustive state search, proof explanation, and verifier/package preparation.

open_questions.question: Can an odd-order class-two address group outside Q8/D8 admit a central target whose two-register shared word is shorter than its direct per-register words?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This package shows no sharing gain for the smallest exponent-three Heisenberg target; a different group may have a longer direct commutator word and leave room for a real call reduction.
open_questions.first_step: Specify one finite group and generator alphabet, then prove the target word metric and direct multi-register bill before searching rank-one register words.
open_questions.blocked_by: The next candidate must avoid the current Q8, D8, UT4 and affine-register overlaps and must have an explicit physical or supplier-level relevance.
